item.title: Colorado has logged more than 7,000 bear sightings in 2026, topping its previous full-year record
item.description: In recent months, severe drought conditions in the American West have driven malnourished bears into urban areas in search of food. With natural vegetation dwindling, bears have turned to human settlements, often scavenging through trash cans. These encounters, which typically start with easily preventable issues like unsecured rubbish bins or unattended bird feeders, are becoming more frequent as the population grows in the region. Las labores de rescate continúan, especialmente en un túnel hidroeléctrico donde se cree que permanecen atrapados unos 100 trabajadores, mientras Nepal realiza entierros de víctimas sin identificar. item.title: Hundreds of hidden earthquakes found at Antarctica’s Doomsday Glacier
item.description: Hundreds of previously overlooked seismic events have been detected beneath Antarctica, including 245 near the marine edge of the Thwaites Glacier. Many appear to be glacial earthquakes caused when huge icebergs break off, capsize, and collide with the glacier. The surge in activity coincided with a period when Thwaites was flowing faster toward the ocean, hinting that changing ocean conditions may be destabilizing the ice. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Northern spotted owl once became a symbol of America’s logging wars; now scientists say it is already functionally extinct
item.description: The northern spotted owl, once a revered icon of environmental activism, faces dire circumstances as it becomes functionally extinct in numerous regions. A recent study indicates a severe decline in its populations throughout their historical habitat. Factors such as habitat destruction and rampant wildfires have severely impacted the species over the years, while the encroaching barred owl emerges as a formidable threat. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

Like tens of thousands of Nepalese people in recent days, she went to one of the country’s medical centres to find out whether her husband was among those whose bodies had been recovered in recent days. item.description: Rescue and relief efforts in Nepal and Tibet have been hampered this Sunday by heavy rain and rising river levels. The latest figures following Wednesday’s flash floods put the death toll at 750, while more than 3,000 people remain missing. Nepal’s disaster authorities are urging rescue teams to “exercise caution”, warning that bad weather, swollen rivers and the threat of further flooding could hamper operations. Shazab Wahlah reports from the town of Bidur. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Nepal-Tibet floods: 750 dead, 20,000 deployed as rising rivers hamper rescue ops
item.description: Nepal and Tibet floods have claimed 750 lives and left over 3,000 missing. Rescuers continue operations amid warnings of fresh flooding and difficult conditions. Hundreds are believed trapped in hydropower tunnels, requiring specialized international assistance. India and China are providing crucial support including forensic experts and relief supplies. Infrastructure damage has cut off communities, while aid efforts are ongoing. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: China-Nepal floods: hundreds of foreigners missing in Tibet after disaster
item.description: China said on Sunday that 261 foreign citizens were missing after last week’s deadly floods along the border between its Tibet autonomous region and Nepal. The missing foreigners were from 23 different countries and included 104 Nepalese citizens, authorities in Tibet’s Gyirong county told reporters. Also unaccounted for are 49 people from India; 33 Latvians; 18 from the United States; 15 from Britain; six each from Canada and Australia; four from South Africa; three each from Malaysia, Germany... item.title: The next Cascadia megaquake could hit Oregon harder than expected
item.description: The Juan de Fuca plate beneath northern Oregon appears to be shallower than previously estimated, potentially making shaking from a future Cascadia megathrust earthquake significantly stronger. item.title: Fire in California’s Big Sur region doubles in size overnight, forcing evacuations
item.description: Plaskett fire has swept through more than 5,900 acres in Monterey county and remains un-contained, says Cal Fire A fire in California’s Big Sur region doubled in size overnight, forcing the evacuation of nearby residents, in a coastal region where firefighters have battled another blaze for weeks. The Plaskett fire, which sparked on Tuesday, had swept through more than 5,900 acres (2,400 hectares) in Monterey county as of Friday, and remained un-contained, according to Cal Fire. item.title: Jesús Revuelto: "Cambio climático podría hacer que se repita la riada de Nepal en otro lugar"
item.description: La riada que ocurrió en Nepal deja en evidencia el riesgo que corren alrededor de 15 millones de personas ante la amenaza de los llamados lagos glaciares, un cuerpo de agua formado a partir del retroceso del glaciar. Poblaciones ubicadas a las faldas del Himalaya o en la Cordillera de los Andes se encuentran en riesgo. Los efectos del cambio climático han acelerado el retroceso o derretimiento de las formaciones de hielo, que a nivel global han perdido altos porcentajes de su masa. Para analizar el tema, hablamos con Jesús Revuelto, investigador del Instituto Pirenaico de Ecología… Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: La peor señal de los incendios en España no es que ardan los montes: es que el fuego se está comiendo los cultivos
item.description: Durante mucho tiempo, la imagen mental que teníamos de un incendio forestal se limitaba a unas llamas que devoraban masas de árboles en los más profundo de un bosque o en la ladera de una montaña. Pero la realidad de los incendios en España ha cambiado drásticamente y el fuego ya no arde solo en el monte, sino que ahora devora con virulencia los antiguos campos de cultivo que antes servían de escudo natural. Y la culpa de todo esto está en el éxodo rural y el abandono de la 'España vaciada'. Lo que teníamos.
